messages:
alex: Heads up — running long-context stress on Qwen-MQA (1.1b) with rope_scale=1.5 and we see KV memory climb steadily, plus lots of 4k page evictions after ~45k tokens. profiler attached below. :eyes:

mira: Can you paste the profiler snippet? is this on dedicated or local dev VM?

alex: Dedicated-dev pool, gpus: a100-80gb. snippet:```
KV pages: total=128k used=112k fragmented=18k
Eviction events: count=412 last=2026-03-21T10:11:05Z
Avg page reuse latency=1.8ms
Top alloc sites: rope_scale_transform, kv_insert, kv_compact
Mem growth: +28GB over 50k tokens
```

jonathan: Interesting — rope_scale 1.5 will change the rot matrix indices, could be causing more unique keys per position and preventing reuse. MQA means multiple heads per token; combined could blow up KV map cardinality.

sophie: Is this specific to Qwen or do we see similar on Mistral/Llama?

alex: Mistral didn't show the same steady growth on identical prompts, Llama had intermittent fragmentation but lower eviction rate. Qwen is worst.

mira: Two quick hypotheses: 1) kernel selection path for Qwen is choosing an allocation-heavy implementation for KV ops; 2) our page compaction trigger threshold is too high for the observed allocation pattern.

perf-bot: flamegraph: https://perf.example/internal/fg/1772456789 (sampled 120s) — shows heavy time in kv_insert and rope_index_compute.

jonathan: Can you run with rope_scale=1.0 and MQA disabled (or MQA fallback to GQA) to isolate? Also try forcing the compact path every N inserts: set KV_COMPACT_THRESHOLD=128 and retest.

alex: Running variants now. Quick results: rope_scale=1.0 reduces growth slope by ~40%. Disabling MQA reduces peak resident by ~30% and evictions down to ~120. With KV_COMPACT_THRESHOLD=128 evictions almost disappear but CPU goes up ~10%.

mira: That strongly points to fragmentation from per-position unique entries. If smaller thresholds work, we can make compaction dynamic based on sequence length and model-specific heuristics.

jonathan: Also check our kernel selection logs: add DEBUG_KERN=1 and look for fallback to generic kv kernels on Qwen token lengths > 2048. Could be the optimized path isn't selecting due to rope scaling math producing odd stride sizes.

alex: Added DEBUG_KERN log: saw we hit generic_kv_write at around seq=4096. Optimized kernel requires stride mod 64 == 0, rope_scale variant changed effective stride.

sophie: Maybe we should add a small pre-pass that normalizes rope indices (quantize to nearest even stride) so optimized kernels still match? We need to be careful about correctness though.

mira: Agreed. As interim we can: 1) tune KV_COMPACT_THRESHOLD per-model (lower for Qwen-MQA long-context), 2) add a runtime metric to detect rising fragmentation and trigger async compaction, 3) instrument kernel selector to prefer optimized kernels when safe.

alex: I'll open a short-lived feature flag to lower compaction threshold for qwen-* variants and add the async compactor job. Also adding a perf test in nightly with 100k token scenarios.

jonathan: Note to self: validate correctness if we alter rope index normalization. Add unit test comparing attention outputs before/after normalization for a few seeds.

perf-bot: Created perf ticket INF-5123 with attached logs and flamegraph.

alex: Action items assigned: alex -> flag + async compactor, mira -> kernel selector tweak PR, jonathan -> unit tests for normalization, sophie -> add long-context nightly. We'll reconvene after nightly run. :thumbsup:

mira: Thanks — if nightly shows improvement we can promote flag to default for qwen in Dedicated.

sophie: Recording the experiment notes in runbook and linking to INF-5123.

alex: closing for now, will post results 1st thing tomorrow.
